To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the engagement of HHLA‐DR molecules by monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) triggers a cascade of intracellular signaling events in metastatic melanomas.

the engagement of HLa‐DR molecules expressed by melanoma cells induces functional intracellular signaling, which is consistent with evidence obtained in hematological neoplasms, and suggests the possibility of using HLA‐DR to set‐up targeted therapies in cutaneous melanomas.

the engagement of Hla‐DR molecules by anti‐HLA class II antibodies induces functional intracellular signals in melanoma cells, including the inhibition of cell growth, homotypic aggregation, and tyrosine phosphorylating of multiple proteins and inhibition of activator protein‐DNA binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel molecular targets for the development of targeted therapies against melanoma.
the role played by HLA class II (HLA‐DR) molecules in melanoma.
the role of human leukocytes antigens (HLAs) in the biology of melanoma, with a particular focus on the HLA‐DR antigens, the only class II molecules expressed by melanocytes and melanoma cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the engagement of Hla‐DR molecules by L243 mAb induces functional intracellular signals in metastatic melanomas.
HLA‐DR can transduce functional signals in melanoma cells.
the engagement of HLa‐DR molecules by anti‐HLA DR antibodies is a novel and potentially useful approach to inhibit the growth of melanoma cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the engagement of human leukocyte antigen (HLA)‐DR molecules expressed by cutaneous melanoma cells induces intracellular signals.

the engagement of HLa‐DR molecules by specific mAbs transduce functional intracellulary signals in melanoma cells, including the activation of the tyrosine kinase‐dependent pathway, and inhibition of AP‐1‐DNA.
HLA‐DR is a targetable molecule in metastatic melanomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HLA‐DR, a molecule that was thought to be only a marker of antigen presentation, can transduce intracellular signals in cutaneous metastatic melanoma.
the engagement of Hla‐DR molecules on melanoma cells transduces functional signals, and this may be used to design new approaches of targeted immunotherapy for metastatic melanoma.
the engagement of Hla‐DR molecules by a monoclonal antibody triggers intracellular signaling in melanoma cells and inhibits tumor growth and homotypic aggregation.
